title: 空载长线：终端电压为什么比始端高
statement: 一条 600 km、50 Hz 的超高压输电线按无损耗线计算：Z_c = 380 Ω，v = 3×10⁸ m/s。始端相电压保持 U̇_1 = 127∠0° kV（有效值），终端空载（开路）。
x 从始端量起，x′ 从终端量起；İ 的参考方向沿 +x（从始端流向终端）。

questions.ask: 线路中点（x = 300 km）电压 U = ?
始端电流（空载充电电流）I_1 = ?

questions.explain: Z_in 是纯容性（l < λ/4 的开路线），所以 İ_1 超前 U̇_1 90°：初相 90°。

questions.ask: 用行波的观点，空载长线终端电压升高的原因是：
choices: 终端开路时线上只有入射波，而入射波沿线越走越大
终端开路，Γ_2 = 1：入射波和反射波在终端同相相加；往始端走，两者的相位差 2βx′ 增大，合成电压按 cos βx′ 变小
线路电阻上产生了负的压降
choiceExplain: 开路时 Γ_2 = 1，反射波和入射波一样大；无损耗线上入射波的大小处处相同，不会“越走越大”。
电阻只会产生压降；而且这里线路无损耗。
questions.explain: Γ_2 = 1，反射波电压与入射波电压在终端同相相加，U̇_2 = 2U̇_2⁺；在始端两者相差 2βl = 72°，合成的模只有 2U⁺cos 36°，所以 U_1 = U_2 cos βl < U_2。从集总的角度看，这是分布电容的充电电流流过分布电感造成的电压升。

hints: 从终端写方程最方便：开路时 İ_2 = 0，无损耗线方程只剩 U̇(x′) = U̇_2 cos βx′、İ(x′) = jU̇_2 sin βx′/Z_c。
βl = 2πl/λ，λ = v/f = 6000 km。始端条件 U̇_1 = U̇_2 cos βl 定出 U̇_2。
始端电流也可以用输入阻抗 Z_in = −jZ_c cot βl 求；它是纯电抗，所以电流与电压相差 90°。
solution: **3. 沿线分布。** U(x′) = U_2 cos βx′：中点 βx′ = 18°，U = **149.3 kV**；电压从始端到终端单调升高。
**检查：** Z_in = −j380 × cot 36° = −j523.0 Ω，127000/523.0 = 242.8 A ✓。实际电网在空载长线末端装并联电抗器来抑制这种电压升高。

en.title: Unloaded long line: why the end voltage is higher than the start
statement: A 600 km, 50 Hz EHV line is computed as lossless: Z_c = 380 Ω, v = 3×10⁸ m/s. The phase voltage at the start is held at U̇_1 = 127∠0° kV (rms) and the end is unloaded (open).
x is measured from the start and x′ from the end; the reference direction of İ is +x (from the start towards the end).

questions.ask: No-load voltage at the end U_2 = ?
Voltage at the midpoint (x = 300 km) U = ?
questions.explain: U̇(x′) = U̇_2 cos βx′ (x′ from the end); at the midpoint x′ = 300 km, βx′ = 18°: U = 157.0 × cos 18° = 149.3 kV.

questions.ask: Current at the start (no-load charging current) I_1 = ?

questions.explain: Z_in is purely capacitive (an open line shorter than λ/4), so İ_1 leads U̇_1 by 90°: phase 90°.

questions.ask: In travelling-wave terms, why does the voltage rise at the open end of a long line?
choices: With the end open only the incident wave exists, and it grows as it travels
The open end gives Γ_2 = 1: incident and reflected waves add in phase at the end; towards the start their phase difference 2βx′ grows and their sum shrinks as cos βx′
The line resistance produces a negative voltage drop
questions.explain: With Γ_2 = 1 the reflected voltage wave adds in phase to the incident one at the end, U̇_2 = 2U̇_2⁺; at the start they are 2βl = 72° apart and their sum is only 2U⁺cos 36°, so U_1 = U_2 cos βl < U_2. In lumped terms: the charging current of the distributed capacitance flowing through the distributed inductance raises the voltage.
choiceExplain: With the end open Γ_2 = 1, so the reflected wave is as large as the incident one; and on a lossless line the incident wave has the same amplitude everywhere — it does not grow.
Right: |U̇(x′)| = 2U⁺|cos βx′|, largest at the end.
Resistance can only cause a voltage drop; and this line is lossless.

hints: Writing the equations from the end is easiest: with the end open İ_2 = 0, so the lossless line equations reduce to U̇(x′) = U̇_2 cos βx′, İ(x′) = jU̇_2 sin βx′/Z_c.
βl = 2πl/λ with λ = v/f = 6000 km. The start condition U̇_1 = U̇_2 cos βl gives U̇_2.
The start current also follows from the input impedance Z_in = −jZ_c cot βl; it is a pure reactance, so current and voltage are 90° apart.
solution: **3. Along the line.** U(x′) = U_2 cos βx′: at the midpoint βx′ = 18°, U = **149.3 kV**; the voltage rises steadily from the start to the end.
**4. Charging current.** İ_1 = jU̇_2 sin βl/Z_c = j157.0 × 0.5878/380 = **j242.8 A** (leading U̇_1 by **90°**); the line only absorbs reactive power.
**Check:** Z_in = −j380 × cot 36° = −j523.0 Ω, 127000/523.0 = 242.8 A ✓. Real grids connect shunt reactors at the end of long unloaded lines to limit this rise.
